title: Bounded exact-term Hom preserves quasi-isomorphisms
statement: Let $J$ be a Grothendieck topology on a small category $C$, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $P$ a cochain complex of sheaves of $R$-modules. Suppose $P^n=0$ outside a finite interval and that each functor $\mathcal Hom_R(P^n,-)$ sends short exact sequences to short exact sequences. For every quasi-isomorphism $f:M\to N$ of arbitrary cochain complexes [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules], the induced map $\mathcal Hom^\bullet_R(P,M)\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet_R(P,N)$ [def-pur-hom-complex] is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 08DM (cohomology-lemma-RHom-strictly-perfect), bounded Hom calculation; homology.tex Tag 0117 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain) for finite-filtration induction

proof.text: For P concentrated in degree k, the product and differential formulas of def-pur-hom-complex identify Hom(P,M) with the shifted complex obtained by applying internal Hom from P^k degreewise. Postcomposition is additive. Preservation of short exact sequences gives an exact functor: factor any differential through its image and apply the short exact sequences for its kernel and image. The equivalence of short-exact preservation with exactness is lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology. The natural cohomology comparison of lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology then shows preservation of quasi-isomorphisms.

Let T_k be the stupid tail of P in degrees at least k and G_k=P^k placed in degree k. The sequence 0 to T_{k+1} to T_k to G_k to 0 is degreewise split. From the product projections and differential of def-pur-hom-complex, restriction and extension by zero give the degreewise split sequence 0 to Hom(G_k,M) to Hom(T_k,M) to Hom(T_{k+1},M) to 0, compatible with the maps induced by f. Repeat for N.

Use the natural long exact sequences of lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact and apply lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma to the five consecutive terms centered on each cohomology of Hom(T_k,-). If the maps for G_k and T_{k+1} are quasi-isomorphisms, so is the map for T_k. Starting with the zero tail above b, descend finitely to a; the omitted degrees below a are zero. The first step handles each G_k. If b<a, P and both Hom complexes are zero. Finite support makes all products effectively finite despite unbounded M and N.
